title: Cyclic fibers and exponential lower bounds for Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constants

definitions.name: x2611_15210_s
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_15210_s (L : ℕ) (G : Type*) [AddCommMonoid G] : ℕ :=
  sInf {s : ℕ | ∀ a : Fin s → G, ∃ I : Finset (Fin s), I.card = L ∧ ∑ i ∈ I, a i = 0}
definitions.notes: Generalized zero-sum constant s_L(G): least length s at which every positional sequence has an L-position zero-sum. The sInf convention outside the paper’s domain is immaterial; every use is for positive L divisible by the exponent of a finite group. This also gives the paper’s rank-zero convention.

definitions.name: x2611_15210_A
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_15210_A (L : ℕ) (G : Type*) [AddCommMonoid G] : ℕ :=
  x2611_15210_s L G - 1
definitions.notes: The paper’s A_L(G)=s_L(G)-1, with natural subtraction. Every use has L≥2, so this is the maximum length of an L-term-zero-sum-free sequence in the paper’s domain.

definitions.name: x2611_15210_rho
definitions.notes: The rho_m of Theorems 1.2 and 4.2. All fractional powers are real powers, and the binomial coefficient is computed in ℕ then cast to ℝ.

definitions.name: x2611_15210_alpha
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_15210_alpha (β : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  sInf {a : ℝ | 0 < a ∧ a ^ 5 = 12 * a + 8 * β}
definitions.notes: The least positive real root of a^5=12a+8beta, expressed by sInf. For beta>1, existence and uniqueness and alpha>2 are asserted in Theorem 3.1. This definition asserts no existence on its own.

definitions.name: x2611_15210_rho_prime
definitions.notes: The rho prime of Corollary 4.4, using real fractional powers.

definitions.name: x2611_15210_Q
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_15210_Q (n m K : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (K + 1), (n.choose (j * m) : ℝ) * p ^ (j * m) * (1 - p) ^ (n - j * m)
definitions.notes: The probability polynomial in (1.3), with K explicit. Statements impose n=Km. Finset.range(K+1) includes j=K.

definitions.name: x2611_15210_P
definitions.notes: Exactly the nine binary vectors in (4.1), indexed 0 through 8 in the order P1 through P9.

definitions.name: x2611_15210_binary_witness
definitions.lean:
def x2611_15210_binary_witness (m r L : ℕ) (B : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → Fin r → ZMod m),
    B ≤ (N : ℝ) ∧ (∀ i j, a i j = 0 ∨ a i j = 1) ∧
    ∀ I : Finset (Fin N), I.card = L → ∑ i ∈ I, a i ≠ 0
definitions.notes: Existence of a positional sequence of length at least the real bound B, supported on {0,1}^r in C_m^r, with no L-position zero-sum. Repeated values are allowed.

statements.name: x2611_15210_thm1_2
statements.original:
Let $m\geq 3$ be odd, and define $\rho_{m}>1$ and $\alpha_{m}>2$ by

 $\rho_{m}=\left(\frac{9^{2m}}{9+36\binom{2m}{m}}\right)^{1/(5(2m-1))},\qquad\alpha_{m}^{5}=12\alpha_{m}+8\rho_{m}.$ 

Then, for every $r\geq 1$ ,

(1.2)

 $\mathsf{s}_{2m}(C_{m}^{r})\ \geq\ \frac{m}{12e}\,\rho_{m}^{r}+1,\qquad\mathsf{s}(C_{2m}^{r})\ \geq\ \frac{m}{12e}\Bigl(\frac{2}{\alpha_{m}}\Bigr)^{4}\alpha_{m}^{r}+1.$ 

Moreover, $\rho_{m}\geq\rho_{3}=3^{6/25}=1.3016945937\ldots$ and hence
 $\alpha_{m}\geq\alpha_{3}=2.0341017978\ldots$ for all odd $m\geq 3$ , and

 $\lim_{\begin{subarray}{c}m\to\infty\\
m\text{ odd}\end{subarray}}\rho_{m}=(9/2)^{1/5}=1.3509600385\ldots,\qquad\lim_{\begin{subarray}{c}m\to\infty\\
m\text{ odd}\end{subarray}}\alpha_{m}=2.0394244419\ldots.$
statements.notes: rho is exactly the printed ratio with a real exponent. alpha(beta) selects the least positive root of x^5 = 12x + 8beta; the assertions include its defining equation and > 2. Odd-modulus limits use m = 2k+1. The final alpha limit is characterized by the same root at beta=(9/2)^(1/5), as explained in the proof of Theorem 1.2; the displayed decimals with ellipses are annotations, not equalities to truncated decimals.

statements.label: Lemma 2.1
statements.name: x2611_15210_lem2_1
statements.original:
Let $L\geq 2$ , let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $\exp(G)\mid L$ , and let
 $\mu$ be a probability distribution on $G$ . Suppose that the sum of $L$ 
independent samples from $\mu$ is zero with probability $\theta>0$ . Put

 $D_{L}=\bigl((L-1)!\bigr)^{1/(L-1)},\qquad N=\bigl\lfloor D_{L}\,\theta^{-1/(L-1)}\bigr\rfloor.$ 

Then $A_{L}(G)\geq(1-1/L)N$ . If $L\geq 4$ , then also

 $A_{L}(G)\ \geq\ \frac{L}{4e}\,\theta^{-1/(L-1)}.$

For every odd integer $m\geq 3$ , put

(4.2)

 $q_{m}=\frac{9+36\binom{2m}{m}}{9^{2m}},\qquad\rho_{m}=q_{m}^{-1/(5(2m-1))}.$

(4.3)

 $A_{2m}(C_{m}^{r})\ \geq\ \Bigl(1-\frac{1}{2m}\Bigr)\Bigl\lfloor\bigl((2m-1)!\bigr)^{1/(2m-1)}\rho_{m}^{5t}\Bigr\rfloor.$ 

Moreover, for every $r\geq 0$ ,

(4.4)

 $A_{2m}(C_{m}^{r})\ \geq\ \frac{m}{12e}\,\rho_{m}^{r}\ \geq\ \frac{m}{12e}\,3^{6r/25}.$ 

The witnessing sequences may be chosen in $\{0,1\}^{r}$ . Finally,

 $3^{6/25}=\rho_{3}\ \leq\ \rho_{m}\ \leq\ 9^{1/5},\qquad\lim_{\begin{subarray}{c}m\to\infty\\
m\text{ odd}\end{subarray}}\rho_{m}=(9/2)^{1/5}.$
